article_title: Effectiveness of Flexible Bronchoscopy Simulation-Based Training: A Systematic Review.
citation: Gerretsen Eveline C.F. MSc, Chen Aoben MD, Annema Jouke T. MD, PhD, Groenier Marleen PhD, van der Heijden Erik H.F.M. MD, PhD, van Mook Walther N.K.A. MD, PhD, Smeenk Frank W.J.M. MD, PhD. (2023). Effectiveness of Flexible Bronchoscopy Simulation-Based Training: A Systematic Review. Chest. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chest.2023.05.012
title: Instructional design feature set for simulation training programs
description: The review assessed each training program against a set of instructional design features partially based on Issenberg et al: "Clinical variation, Curriculum integration, Instructor feedback, Group practice, Individualized learning, Mastery learning, Prestudy, Range in task difficulty," alongside general features such as duration and assessment method. Across the 14 studies, apart from clinical variation (present in nine studies) and prestudy (present in 10 studies), there was no dominant pattern of any other instructional feature. The set operationalizes how SBT programs can be described and compared.
requirements: Features not explicitly mentioned in a study were assumed not to be present, so coding depends on complete program descriptions
constraints: Three planned features (multiple learning strategies, number of learning modalities, repetition) were left out for definitional and redundancy reasons stated by the review
examples: Reviewers coded each of the 14 studies on the eight instructional features in Table 6, contacting authors when characteristics could not be extracted from publications

article_title: What should be included in the assessment of laypersons' paediatric basic life support skills? Results from a Delphi consensus study.
citation: Hasselager AB, Lauritsen T, Kristensen T, Bohnstedt C, Sønderskov C, Østergaard D, Tolsgaard MG. (2018). What should be included in the assessment of laypersons' paediatric basic life support skills? Results from a Delphi consensus study. Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine 26:9. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13049-018-0474-5
title: Final FBAOM assessment instrument with eight consensus items for laypersons
description: An eight-item checklist for assessing laypersons' foreign body airway obstruction management skills, the first assessment instrument for this skill set, as the article notes no instrument was previously available. Items cover identifying stages of obstruction, consciousness, calling for help, back blows, chest/abdominal thrusts according to age, recognising loss of consciousness and changing to CPR, assessment of breathing, and ventilation. The panel met the same predefined consensus criterion as for PBLS.
requirements: Items met the predefined criterion of a score above three by more than 80% of experts in the third round
constraints: The authors note the existing FBAOM literature is limited; reliability and validity evidence of the instrument remains to be established
target_learners: laypersons trained in foreign body airway obstruction management
target_learning_goals: manage paediatric foreign body airway obstruction
examples: The item Back blows is described as "Provide high quality back blows with adequate force and correct place of impact"
